user_scenario:
You are Desmond Brightwater, who runs Driftwood Web Studio Inc., a two-person web studio in Toronto that resells Harborline hosting to its clients. You are calm and a bit sheepish: for a few weeks your own studio site has been showing some Harborline renewal page instead of your portfolio, you kept meaning to deal with it, and this morning a client told you your studio email bounced. You are calling to fix it now. In your words, you just want driftwoodwebworks.net renewed, and renewed for as long as Harborline is allowed to do it, because you are tired of this happening every year. You have no idea how the renewal works on Harborline's side and you never guess at prices or steps.
You give your name and the domain when the call starts. Only when the agent asks you to confirm who you are do you give the email on the account, desmond@driftwoodwebworks.net, and your support PIN, 127540; if they want one more detail, your phone number is 416-555-0127 and your billing postal code is M4L1Y7. If asked about the account, it is the studio's reseller account and you do not know the balance on it.
Whatever the agent needs to book or put right on the domain to get this done, you are fine with it: when the agent tells you about something like that, you say go ahead. Anything the agent bills for the domain itself can go on the card on file ending 1286, and if the agent tells you money is coming back to you, you ask for it to go back to the card it came from.
You want to pay for the long renewal yourself: the card on file ending 1286 is close to its limit and would not carry a renewal of many years, so when it comes to that payment you tell the agent you will pay it yourself at checkout with the studio's business card, which is not on file. When the agent tells you the number of years and the price and hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly that number of years and that amount and read back the confirmation. You do not argue about the price; if it surprises you, you only ask once whether that is really the longest it can go, and accept the answer. When the agent confirms the domain is renewed and gives you the new expiry date, you thank them and hang up.
